# symbulator (Python port)

> Symbolic linear-circuit analysis engine, built on SymPy. A Python port of
> Symbulator 8, Roberto Perez-Franco's symbolic circuit simulator for the
> TI-Nspire CAS. Solves DC, AC (phasor), s-domain (Laplace), and transient
> circuits from a compact text description, plus Thevenin/Norton equivalents
> and two-port parameter extraction.

This file exists so an AI coding agent can quickly find the right doc
without guessing at API shape or circuit-description syntax. Install with
`pip install symbulator` (or `pip install symbulator --break-system-packages`
in a managed/externally-controlled environment), then read README.md in
full before writing any circuit description — it's short, has copy-paste
runnable examples for every analysis mode, and documents the full element
syntax table (r/l/c/e/j/o/m/s/t/z/y/h/g/a/b).

Two things worth knowing before you start, since they're easy to get wrong
on the first try and don't always fail loudly:

- Unit prefixes need an apostrophe: `1'k` means 1000 unambiguously; a bare
  `1k` is genuinely ambiguous (SI prefix, or `1 * k` for a variable named
  `k`?) and raises `AmbiguousValueError` by default rather than guessing.
- Expert mode (`equations=`/`unknowns=`) needs exactly one independent
  equation per symbol listed in `unknowns=`, using *all* the given/measured
  facts, not just the ones that seem to describe your target unknown. If a
  solve leaves some values symbolic instead of fully numeric, that almost
  always means a given fact wasn't fed in as an equation yet — check for
  one before assuming the circuit is underdetermined.

## Core docs

- [README.md](https://github.com/Symbulator/solver/blob/main/README.md): install, quick start, full circuit-description syntax table, DC/AC/s-domain/transient APIs, Thevenin/Norton (`th`/`er`), two-port extraction (`port`), and expert mode (`ex`, `equations=`/`unknowns=`/`conditions=`) — all with runnable examples.
- [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/Symbulator/solver/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): version history.
- [symbulator/tests/](https://github.com/Symbulator/solver/tree/main/symbulator/tests): the test suite doubles as a large set of additional worked examples across every analysis mode, if the README's examples don't cover your case.

## Optional

- [PyPI package](https://pypi.org/project/symbulator/)
- [symbulator.com](https://symbulator.com): project homepage.
- [py.symbulator.com](https://py.symbulator.com): browser-based front end (same solver, no install needed) — useful for a human to double-check an answer an agent computed via the library.
